issues.description: No CSP has been detected in the target application
issues.consequence: Without a Content Security Policy, injected markup can run inline script. A strict CSP is what turns an HTML injection into a harmless one.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets

issues.description: Missing navigation limits: no will-navigate handler and no setWindowOpenHandler
issues.consequence: Windows can be navigated to any site (e.g. by a link in shared content); that site then runs inside the app window, with its preload and IPC access.
issues.interaction: A click on a crafted link

issues.description: Missing PermissionRequestHandler to limit specific permissions (e.g. openExternal) in response to events from particular origins.
issues.consequence: Without a permission handler, any page (including one reached through a link in shared content) gets camera, microphone, notifications and other permissions automatically.
issues.interaction: Viewing the content is enough when it runs as script; a click when it is a link

issues.description: No Electron Fuses configuration found. RunAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS, --inspect and ASAR integrity fuses are insecure by default
issues.consequence: Build hardening left at insecure defaults. It matters to someone who can start or modify the app on the device (e.g. RunAsNode turns it into a Node.js interpreter), not to other users' content.
issues.interaction: Access to the user's device or account
issues.howToValidate: Manual, local access only: set the fuses in the build (@electron/fuses). Content from other users cannot use them.

issues.description: No certificate pinning found (session.setCertificateVerifyProc); consider pinning the certificates of the backends the application trusts
issues.consequence: Without certificate pinning, a certificate from any trusted authority (e.g. a corporate TLS proxy) can intercept the app's traffic.
issues.interaction: None: an attacker on the network path acts while the app talks to its servers

issues.description: IPC handler does not appear to validate the sender (event.senderFrame) before acting on the message
issues.consequence: The IPC handler does not check which page sent the message: script injected into any window, or a foreign page the window navigated to, can call it with the app's privileges.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets
issues.howToValidate: Manual: read the handler and check that it verifies event.senderFrame (its URL or origin) before acting. A watch session lists the origins that used each channel, and whether content carrying the marker reached it.

issues.consequence: What a page can make the main process do through this channel: script injected into a window that can reach it inherits these capabilities.
issues.interaction: None of its own: it decides how far content that is already injected gets

issues.description: DevTools are opened programmatically; ensure this cannot happen in production builds (always opened, including in production builds)
issues.consequence: DevTools can be opened in the shipped app: someone at the keyboard can inspect and run code in the app's context. Other users' content cannot use this.
issues.interaction: Access to the user's device or account

issues.description: Gets the electron version used by inspecting the package.json file.
issues.consequence: The Electron version the findings are based on.
